content.text:
Partial: MissingBulbWebsite, EdFringeNow and Canary are on `60830.9` with the fixed rule; VascularColoring and hitbut are still on `.5`. `fleet-baseline` is mid-flight, so I'll let it finish before waking. Meanwhile — your question.

## Why 91 decision vs 26 approval

Partly real, partly a labelling artifact — and you were right to be suspicious.

**The artifact:** [MissingBulbWebsite #240](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/issues/240) is labelled `task:needs-human-decision`, but it holds open **PR #246** and its own final comment says *"Waiting on a person: merge or close #246, then close this item."* It should be an `approval`. It isn't, because the session couldn't run `converge-item.mjs --outcome approval --pr 246` — that script needs Action-level REST access and an agentic session is MCP-only. The convergence never happened, so the item never received its approval outcome and fell back to a decision park.

So an unknown slice of the 91 are approvals-with-PRs that failed to converge. The kind split is not a reliable proxy for "has a PR".

**The real part:** counting open PRs against R5 items:

| repo | R5 items | open PRs |
|---|---:|---:|
| Claudinite | 22 | 15 |
| hitbut | 16 | 3 |
| MissingBulbWebsite | 12 | 4 |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | 11 | 6 |
| VascularColoring | 10 | 2 |
| **total** | **71** | **30** |

So roughly **40% of R5 holds a PR**; the majority are genuinely questions with no artifact attached — a worker asking "should I treat X as Y?" before producing anything.

**But your instinct is exactly right where it counts.** Claudinite's `canon-curation/growth-promote` stack is 8 parked items — and there are **9 open "Promote lessons from…" PRs** sitting beside them (#1451, #1419, #1409, #1372, #1345, #1303, #1204, #1157, #1021). That is precisely the repeat-PR pattern you described, and they almost certainly overlap heavily: each run re-scans the same member local packs, and the earlier lesson is still there *because the earlier PR never merged*.

## On the proposal

The direction is right and the payoff you name is real — one review, one approval, many items closing. Three things I'd change before building it.

**1. "Append" is the wrong operation; "recompute onto the same branch" is the right one.** `growth-promote`'s output isn't additive text, it's a derived answer to *"what should canon hold, given member packs today."* If run 5 appends to run 1's branch you get the same lesson written twice, and any lesson run 1 proposed that run 5 would now reject stays in the diff. Rebuilding the output on the existing branch gives you one PR that is always current, which is strictly better and no harder.

**2. It fixes the PRs but not the item count.** There are 8 items because a non-blocking park frees the standing slot and the generator files a fresh occurrence next anchor. Collapsing the PRs leaves 8 open work items each still needing a close. The duplication has to be stopped at the generator, not downstream.

**3. Unbounded batching can make review worse, not better.** A PR that accumulates for three weeks is one large all-or-nothing diff. Today you can merge one promote PR and close another; batched, you can't split the judgment.

So the smaller, more direct fix is at the generator:

> **Don't file a new occurrence of a task whose previous occurrence is still parked holding an unresolved PR.**

That gives you one live run, therefore one PR, therefore one item — no per-task rework, and the machinery already exists: [#1472](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1472) already stamps `Ends-when: #<n> closed` on a park given a `--pr`, and rule G already closes the item when that PR resolves. The missing half is just "don't re-file while it's open."

The cost you'd be accepting: a task whose PR sits unreviewed for a month stops running for a month. For `growth-promote` that's harmless — the next run re-derives everything. For a sweep whose value is time-sensitive it isn't, so I'd scope it to tasks whose `expected_outcome` is a PR.

Branch reuse then becomes a *complement* for the few tasks where content genuinely accumulates, not the primary mechanism.

options.label: Gate the generator on an unresolved PR (Recommended)
options.description: Don't file a new occurrence of a task whose previous occurrence is still parked holding an open PR. One live run → one PR → one item. Reuses #1472's Ends-when stamp and rule G, so it's a small change at one place in the generator rather than per-task rework. Fixes both the 58 duplicate items and the 9 stacked promote PRs at their shared root. Cost: a task whose PR sits unreviewed stops running until it's resolved — scoped to tasks whose expected_outcome is a PR.

options.label: Recompute onto the existing branch
options.description: Your proposal, with append replaced by rebuild: a task finding an unresolved prior instance checks out that branch and regenerates its output there. One always-current PR per task. Does NOT reduce the open item count on its own — each run still files and parks its own item — so it needs the generator gate anyway to stop the item pile.

options.label: Both — gate first, branch reuse for growth-promote
options.description: Land the generator gate as the general fix, then add branch reuse only for canon-curation/growth-promote, where content genuinely accumulates across runs and the 8-item/9-PR stack is worst. Two changes, sequenced, with the second informed by whether the first already suffices.

`fleet-baseline` delivered `60830.9` to 12 of 14. I woke the janitor on all of those and fired `update` on the two stragglers.

| repo | before | after | R4 closed |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| MissingBulbWebsite | 16 | 13 | #170, #156, #153 |

[EdFringeNow #359](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/issues/359) closed `task:status:rejected` at 22:39:36 — the rename worked exactly as intended. And Canary **#115**, the item that started [#1461](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1461), is finally gone.

[VascularColoring #109](https://github.com/missingbulb/VascularColoring/issues/109) hasn't closed yet — that repo is still on `60830.5` and hasn't taken the update. But the rename already did its job: the item now carries `task:status:needs-human-failure` instead of a bare `needs-human`, meaning it is in the queue and will close on its next sweep.

## 2. The mislabelling — I was wrong, and it's worse than mislabelling

I said the decision/approval split reflected worker judgment. It doesn't. `queue-sweep.mjs:95`:

```js
await escalate(item, deadAgentComment(...), STATUS_RUNNING_AGENT, NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION);
```

**Janitor rule B hardcodes `decision` for every dead agent claim.** Nobody chose it.

I then read five decision parks across five repos and tasks. All five follow the identical arc:

1. Agent claims the item and **does the work correctly**
2. It cannot run `converge-item.mjs` — MCP-only session, no Action `GITHUB_TOKEN`
3. It correctly refuses to hand-fake the transition, and says so
4. The claim goes stale at 3h
5. Rule B parks it `decision`

| item | what the agent actually did | true outcome |
|---|---|---|
| [MissingBulbWebsite #240](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/issues/240) | opened PR #246 | `approval` |
| [ClaudiniteWebsite #308](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/issues/308) | opened PR #315 | `approval` |
| [VascularColoring #159](https://github.com/missingbulb/VascularColoring/issues/159) | 0 claims to revalidate, no PR needed | `done` |
| [CrosswordChat #307](https://github.com/missingbulb/CrosswordChat/issues/307) | triaged, verdict `leave` | `done` |
| [Claudinite #1376](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1376) | triaged 5 issues, all `leave` | `done` |

**Not one of the five is a decision you owe anyone.** Three should have closed themselves `done`. Two are approvals holding a finished PR.

So the "91 decisions" is largely not a backlog of questions — it's a **graveyard of successful runs that could not record their own success**.

## 3. This changes the answer to your design question

One defect produces all three symptoms:

- the **91 decisions** — every unconverged agent run lands there
- the **58 duplicate items** — a `decision` park is non-blocking, so the lane frees and the task re-files tomorrow, fails to converge again, parks again
- the **9 stacked promote PRs** — each of those re-runs opens another PR

Branch reuse would tidy the third symptom while leaving the machine still unable to close its own work. I'd not build it yet. Fix `converge-item.mjs`'s session-side path and successful runs close themselves `done`, PR-bearing ones park `approval` with `Ends-when:` so rule G closes them on merge, and the lanes stop re-filing — the duplication disappears rather than being consolidated.

The gap is already filed several times over — [ClaudiniteWebsite #274](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/issues/274), [#277](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/issues/277), [Shepherd #179](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/issues/179), [Canary #239](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/239) — and every one of those was filed by an agent hitting exactly this wall. Your own local pack documents it as a standing rule.

> ⚠️ Still open: **`converge-item.mjs` cannot run session-side** — this is the root cause of R5's shape, the 58 duplicate items and the stacked promote PRs; filed four times across the fleet and never fixed. I have **not** started it. **VascularColoring and hitbut are stuck at `60830.5`** — `update` fired, not yet converged; their R4 items (Vascular #148/#146/#118/#109) clear on the sweep after. **[#1482](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1482)** — #1466 shipped without a version bump; the `pack-version-bumped` check should have caught it and didn't. **R5 ≈ 128 still standing**, but the count is not trustworthy as a measure of work you owe until convergence is fixed and the graveyard drains.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

{"number":1490,"title":"A done terminal closes the issue it stands on, marked or filed","body":"Closes #1489

missingbulb/Shepherd#360 ran, posted its deliverable, took `task:status:done` — and stayed **open**, with nothing on it for anyone to do. Two separate things had to be true for that, and both are here.

**A `done` terminal closes the issue it stands on.** §16.1/§16.5 said a marked issue is never closed by its own run: the status belongs to the run, the issue's open/closed to its author. That holds for every terminal but one. `done` is the outcome that means nothing is left for anyone to act on, so an issue left open under it is asking its author to come and agree with what the run already settled. It now closes either shape, at all three surfaces that carry the terminal — the session's `convergeOps`, the executor's code-work `close()`, and janitor rule G's *merged* half. Unchanged: a park waits on a person and stays open, and `task:status:rejected` still stands on the open marked issue, because a run's verdict is not the issue's validity. Each of the three has a contrast test pinning that half.

**Converge's membership test accepts an origin label.** It was gated on the machine block — the single artifact it exists to validate — so an item adopted before those delimiters existed read as "not a Claudinite work item". That is what actually happened on Shepherd#360: `converge-item.mjs` refused, the session performed the transition by hand, and the close was the step it dropped. An origin label is the independent signal — every item carries one for life, and applying it is platform-write-gated exactly as the block's adoption was. Any one of the three signals now suffices.

Without the second half the first would not have fired on the item that prompted it.

### What changed, by folder

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/
  converge-item.mjs   the session's convergence: a done outcome always emits the
                      close op; membership accepts an origin label as a third signal
  executor.mjs        close() closes a marked issue on TASK_DONE, still returns
                      early for the rejected terminal

packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/task-janitor/
  queue-sweep.mjs     rule G closes on the RESOLUTION, not the item's shape:
                      merged closes completed, unmerged leaves a marked issue open

docs/tasks-dispatch/
  DESIGN.md           §16.1's sentence and shape table, §16.5's end table — the
                      reversal recorded where the old decision was stated
```

### Proof

Every behavioural change had its test written and watched fail first. Full suite: 2803 pass, 1 fail — `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which fails loudly by design in a shallow checkout and is unrelated. `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` are both 0 blocking.

Whitespace around `&&` canonicalizes away, so the stamped trailer stays one token; an unusable path, a composite or a whole-policy word inside an `&&` term invalidates the policy, which authorizes nothing (#1473). |

The converge stamps `Ends-when: #<n> closed` on any park given a `--pr`, and janitor rule G closes the item when that target resolves — `done` if it merged, `rejected` if it was closed unmerged. input.title: converge-item.mjs is session-only, but carries a REST executor that makes a session report failure
input.body:
`packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/converge-item.mjs` is invoked from exactly one place — `queue/instructions.md` step 6, which only a work-item **session** reads. Nothing else runs it:

- no `.github/workflows/*.yml` names it;
- no module imports `convergeItem`, `convergeOps`, `sessionScript` or `canReachRepo` outside the pack's own tests;
- the Actions side has its own convergence in `queue/executor.mjs` (`converge(...)`), which is untouched by this.

So the file's REST executor is unreachable in practice: the one environment that runs the script is the one environment with no REST route.

## Why this is not merely dead code

`main()` probes for REST first and treats its absence as the fallback branch. A session running step 6 therefore meets a `console.error` and a non-zero exit before it meets the path written for it — and has to re-run with `CLAUDINITE_ITEM_JSON` to get anywhere. Sessions read that first result as breakage and stop, which is exactly what the fleet shows: agents doing the work correctly, reporting they cannot converge, and leaving the item to the janitor's 3h leash. Rule B then parks it `task:status:needs-human-decision` (`queue-sweep.mjs:95`, hardcoded), so a successful run becomes a human park.

Sampled five parked items across five repos and five tasks — [MissingBulbWebsite#240](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/issues/240), [ClaudiniteWebsite#308](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/issues/308), [VascularColoring#159](https://github.com/missingbulb/VascularColoring/issues/159), [CrosswordChat#307](https://github.com/missingbulb/CrosswordChat/issues/307), [Claudinite#1376](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1376). All five are this. Three should have closed `done`; two are approvals holding a finished PR. None is a decision anybody owes an answer to.

The knock-on: a park of kind `decision` does not block its lane, so the standing slot frees and the task re-files on the next anchor, fails to converge again, and parks again. That is the fleet's duplicate-item stacks and its duplicate-PR stacks — one defect, three symptoms.

## The change

State the scope in the file and make the code match it:

- **Header** says plainly that this runs only inside a work-item session, that such a session reaches GitHub through its own tools and never from a subprocess, and that every line here therefore plans a transition the session performs — it never performs one itself.
- **Remove the REST executor** — `convergeItem`, `canReachRepo`, and the `signals/gh.mjs` / `github.mjs` imports. `executor.mjs` already owns the Actions-side transition, so this removes a duplicate, not a capability.
- **One path, one step.** The item is handed in (`--item-file`, the issue as the session's own `issue_read` returned it), the script prints the calls, and printing them is success — exit 0, on stdout.
- **`instructions.md` step 6** rewritten to the two-call shape: read the item, run the command, make the calls it prints.

The planner (`convergeOps`) and the script renderer (`sessionScript`) are unchanged in behaviour; this is about which of them is reachable and what the file says it is for.

Refs #1482

input.body:
Closes #1491

Stacked on #1490 — based on `claude/task-closure-issue-resolution-bgnxsn`, since that PR also edits `converge-item.mjs`. Retarget to `main` once it lands.

## The scope question, answered from the code

`queue/instructions.md` step 6 is this file's **only** caller. No `.github/workflows/*.yml` names it; no module imports `convergeItem`, `convergeOps`, `sessionScript` or `canReachRepo` outside the pack's own tests; the Actions side converges through `executor.mjs`'s own `converge(...)`. It is session-only, so the two scopes were already two files — this one just carried a REST path duplicating the other.

## Why the dead path was not merely dead

`main()` probed for REST first and treated its absence as the fallback. The one environment that runs this script is the one with no REST route, so a session met a `console.error` and a non-zero exit *before* it met the path written for it, then needed a second run behind `CLAUDINITE_ITEM_JSON`.

Sessions read that first result as breakage and stopped. The item kept `task:status:running-agent` until the janitor's 3h leash, and rule B parks a dead claim `needs-human-decision` unconditionally (`queue-sweep.mjs:95`) — so a run that did its work correctly became a human park.

Five items sampled across five repos and five tasks are all exactly this: [MissingBulbWebsite#240](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/issues/240), [ClaudiniteWebsite#308](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/issues/308), [VascularColoring#159](https://github.com/missingbulb/VascularColoring/issues/159), [CrosswordChat#307](https://github.com/missingbulb/CrosswordChat/issues/307), [Claudinite#1376](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1376). Three should have closed `done`; two are approvals holding a finished PR. None is a decision anyone owes an answer to.

And because a `decision` park does not block its lane, the standing slot frees and the task re-files on the next anchor, fails the same way, and parks again — which is where the fleet's duplicate items and duplicate PRs come from. One defect, three symptoms.

## What changed

The header states the scope — one caller, no network, every line assuming MCP — and the code matches it. The file plans a transition and prints it addressed to the session's own tools. **Printing is the success**: stdout, exit 0, never a fallback. The item is handed in with `--item-file` rather than through a second run behind an environment variable; a file rather than an argument because an item's body is prose of arbitrary length and shell-quoting one is a bug waiting for the first apostrophe. `CLAUDINITE_ITEM_JSON` still reads, for a member whose `instructions.md` is a cycle behind.

`convergeOps` and `sessionScript` are unchanged in behaviour.

### By folder

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/
  converge-item.mjs   header states session-only/MCP-only scope; REST executor
                      (convergeItem, canReachRepo) and its signals/gh.mjs and
                      github.mjs imports removed; main() is one path — item in
                      via --item-file, script out on stdout, exit 0
  instructions.md     step 6 rewritten to the two-call shape: read the item,
                      run the command, make the calls it prints
```

## Proof

Every behavioural change had its test written and watched fail first — 3 failing before, 13 passing after in `converge-session.test.mjs`.

`converge-item.test.mjs` keeps **all nineteen** assertions rather than losing them with the executor: they drive the same ops through a local applier, because what they pin — five side effects, in order, once, on the item held and nothing else — is the planner's contract and outlived its transport.

Full CI glob: **2,391 pass, 0 fail**. `check_the_world` 0 blocking; `ci-work-scope --branch` 0 blocking, including the `pack-version-bumped` gate that #1482 caught being skipped — `claudinite-tasks` goes to `60831.2` with its `VERSIONS.md` row.

## What this does not fix

The 128 already-parked R5 items stay parked; this stops new ones being created. Draining the existing pile is separate, and the mislabelled ones need re-reading before anyone treats them as questions.

{"number":1490,"title":"A done terminal closes the issue it stands on, marked or filed","body":"Closes #1489

missingbulb/Shepherd#360 ran, posted its deliverable, took `task:status:done` — and stayed **open**, with nothing on it for anyone to do. Two separate things had to be true for that, and both are here.

**A `done` terminal closes the issue it stands on.** §16.1/§16.5 said a marked issue is never closed by its own run: the status belongs to the run, the issue's open/closed to its author. That holds for every terminal but one. `done` is the outcome that means nothing is left for anyone to act on, so an issue left open under it is asking its author to come and agree with what the run already settled. It now closes either shape, at all three surfaces that carry the terminal — the session's `convergeOps`, the executor's code-work `close()`, and janitor rule G's *merged* half. Unchanged: a park waits on a person and stays open, and `task:status:rejected` still stands on the open marked issue, because a run's verdict is not the issue's validity. Each of the three has a contrast test pinning that half.

**Converge's membership test accepts an origin label.** It was gated on the machine block — the single artifact it exists to validate — so an item adopted before those delimiters existed read as "not a Claudinite work item". That is what actually happened on Shepherd#360: `converge-item.mjs` refused, the session performed the transition by hand, and the close was the step it dropped. An origin label is the independent signal — every item carries one for life, and applying it is platform-write-gated exactly as the block's adoption was. Any one of the three signals now suffices.

Without the second half the first would not have fired on the item that prompted it.

### What changed, by folder

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/
  converge-item.mjs   the session's convergence: a done outcome always emits the
                      close op; membership accepts an origin label as a third signal
  executor.mjs        close() closes a marked issue on TASK_DONE, still returns
                      early for the rejected terminal

packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/task-janitor/
  queue-sweep.mjs     rule G closes on the RESOLUTION, not the item's shape:
                      merged closes completed, unmerged leaves a marked issue open

docs/tasks-dispatch/
  DESIGN.md           §16.1's sentence and shape table, §16.5's end table — the
                      reversal recorded where the old decision was stated
```

### Proof

Every behavioural change had its test written and watched fail first. Full suite: 2803 pass, 1 fail — `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which fails loudly by design in a shallow checkout and is unrelated. `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` are both 0 blocking.

input.body:
Closes #1491

Started stacked on #1490; that merged mid-flight, so this is rebased onto `main` and the diff is this change alone.

## The scope question, answered from the code

`queue/instructions.md` step 6 is this file's **only** caller. No `.github/workflows/*.yml` names it; no module imports `convergeItem`, `convergeOps`, `sessionScript` or `canReachRepo` outside the pack's own tests; the Actions side converges through `executor.mjs`'s own `converge(...)`. It is session-only — so the two scopes were already two files, and this one was just carrying a REST path duplicating the other. No split needed; the header now says which scope this is.

## Why the dead path was not merely dead

`main()` probed for REST first and treated its absence as the fallback. The one environment that runs this script is the one with no REST route, so a session met a `console.error` and a non-zero exit *before* it met the path written for it, then needed a second run behind `CLAUDINITE_ITEM_JSON`.

Sessions read that first result as breakage and stopped. The item kept `task:status:running-agent` until the janitor's 3h leash, and rule B parks a dead claim `needs-human-decision` unconditionally (`queue-sweep.mjs:95`) — so a run that did its work correctly became a human park.

Five items sampled across five repos and five tasks are all exactly this: [MissingBulbWebsite#240](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/issues/240), [ClaudiniteWebsite#308](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/issues/308), [VascularColoring#159](https://github.com/missingbulb/VascularColoring/issues/159), [CrosswordChat#307](https://github.com/missingbulb/CrosswordChat/issues/307), [Claudinite#1376](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1376). Three should have closed `done`; two are approvals holding a finished PR. None is a decision anyone owes an answer to.

And because a `decision` park does not block its lane, the standing slot frees, the task re-files on the next anchor, fails the same way and parks again — which is where the fleet's duplicate items and duplicate PRs come from. One defect, three symptoms.

## What changed

The header states the scope — one caller, no network, every line assuming MCP — and the code matches it. The file plans a transition and prints it addressed to the session's own tools. **Printing is the success**: stdout, exit 0, never a fallback. The item is handed in with `--item-file` rather than through a second run behind an environment variable; a file rather than an argument because an item's body is prose of arbitrary length and shell-quoting one is a bug waiting for the first apostrophe. `CLAUDINITE_ITEM_JSON` still reads, for a member whose `instructions.md` is a cycle behind.

`convergeOps` and `sessionScript` are unchanged in behaviour.

### By folder

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/
  converge-item.mjs   header states the session-only, MCP-only scope; REST
                      executor (convergeItem, canReachRepo) and its
                      signals/gh.mjs and github.mjs imports removed; main() is
                      one path — item in via --item-file, script out on stdout,
                      exit 0
  instructions.md     step 6 rewritten to the two-call shape: read the item,
                      run the command, make the calls it prints
```

## Proof

Every behavioural change had its test written and watched fail first — 3 failing before, 13 passing after in `converge-session.test.mjs`.

`converge-item.test.mjs` keeps **all nineteen** assertions rather than losing them with the executor: they drive the same ops through a local applier, because what they pin — five side effects, in order, once, on the item held and nothing else — is the planner's contract and outlived its transport.

Full CI glob before the rebase: 2,391 pass, 0 fail. After the rebase, the pack's own 327 queue tests pass and `ci-work-scope --branch` reports 0 blocking over the 6 changed files — including the `pack-version-bumped` gate that #1482 caught being skipped. `claudinite-tasks` goes to `60831.2` with its `VERSIONS.md` row.

## What this does not fix

The 128 already-parked R5 items stay parked; this stops new ones being created. Draining the existing pile is separate work, and the mislabelled ones need re-reading before anyone treats them as questions someone owes an answer to.

## Your assumption was right, and the code proves it

`converge-item.mjs` is **session-only**. `queue/instructions.md` step 6 is its only caller — no workflow names it, and nothing imports `convergeItem`, `convergeOps`, `sessionScript` or `canReachRepo` outside the pack's own tests. The Actions side has always converged through `executor.mjs`'s own `converge(...)`.

So **no split was needed** — the two scopes were already two files. This one was just carrying a REST executor that duplicated the other, which is what your "all code should be MCP" instruction resolves to deleting.

## Why that dead path was doing real damage

It wasn't merely unreachable — it was reached **first**. `main()` probed for REST before anything else, so a session hit a `console.error` and a non-zero exit before it ever met the path written for it, and then had to re-run behind `CLAUDINITE_ITEM_JSON`. Sessions read that as breakage and stopped. The 3h leash then fired, and rule B parked a finished run as `needs-human-decision`.

That is the chain behind all five sampled items, the duplicate item stacks, and the duplicate PR stacks.

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/
  converge-item.mjs   header states the session-only, MCP-only scope; REST
                      executor and its signals/gh.mjs + github.mjs imports
                      removed; main() is one path — item in via --item-file,
                      script out on stdout, exit 0
  instructions.md     step 6 rewritten to the two-call shape: read the item,
                      run the command, make the calls it prints
```

## Two judgment calls worth flagging

**I deleted the REST executor rather than leaving it as a documented no-op.** That's my reading of "all code should be MCP" — a second transport nothing can run is what caused this. `executor.mjs` keeps the Actions-side path untouched, so no capability was lost.

**I kept all 19 of `converge-item.test.mjs`'s assertions instead of deleting them with the executor.** They pin the planner's contract — five side effects, in order, once, on the item held — which outlived its transport, so they now drive the same ops through a local applier.

Tests written and watched fail first: 3 failing → 13 passing in `converge-session.test.mjs`. Full glob 2,391 pass before the rebase; `pack-version-bumped` satisfied at `60831.2` with its `VERSIONS.md` row — the gate [#1482](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1482) caught being skipped.

One thing changed under me: **#1490 merged at 09:13, four minutes after I branched off it.** I rebased my single commit onto `main` and dropped its two, so #1493's diff is this change alone.

> ⚠️ Still open: **[#1493](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1493) awaits your review** — CI green (`test-and-conformance` success), [#1491](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1491) closes with it. This **stops new R5 items being created; it does not drain the 128 already parked** — and those need re-reading before being treated as questions you owe answers to, since most are finished runs mislabelled `decision`. **VascularColoring and hitbut are still on `claudinite-tasks 60830.5`** from last night; their `update` was fired but hasn't landed, so their R4 items (Vascular #148/#146/#118/#109) are still waiting on a converge then a janitor run. **[#1482](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1482)** — the `pack-version-bumped` check that let #1466 through unbumped is still unexplained.

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
